nodes.label: Server Component Data Fetching Pattern
nodes.rationale: Public pages use async Server Components that fetch Supabase data at request time via fetchers.ts. On error or no config, seed data is returned as fallback. This enables SSR with graceful degradation.

nodes.label: Seed Data Fallback Architecture
nodes.rationale: Every data fetcher checks isSupabaseConfigured() first. If Supabase is unreachable or unconfigured, hardcoded seed data (menu, hours, venue, gallery) is returned instead of throwing. This makes the site work without a database.

nodes.label: Booking Overlay Portal Pattern
nodes.rationale: BookingOverlay uses React createPortal to render a full-screen modal outside the component tree. It injects an OpenTable iframe dynamically via document.createElement interception to add sandbox attributes. Body scroll is locked via position:fixed. Escape key closes via DOM listener.

nodes.label: OpenTable Widget Sandbox Protection
nodes.rationale: Two-layer navigation guard: (1) Monkey-patched document.createElement adds sandbox attribute to OpenTable's iframe to block window.top navigation. (2) Navigation API guard prevents postMessage-triggered parent-window redirects. This keeps users on the site instead of being redirected to OpenTable.

nodes.label: Supabase Three-Tier Client Architecture
nodes.rationale: Three client types: Browser client (anon key, cookie-based auth), Server client (anon key, next/headers cookies), Admin client (service_role key, bypasses RLS). Browser client is NOT cached at module level to avoid stale refresh tokens after middleware rotation.

nodes.label: ISR On-Demand Revalidation Pattern
nodes.rationale: After every admin save, a POST to /api/admin/revalidate calls revalidatePath on the layout (for shared data like overlay image in Header/Footer) and individual page paths. This ensures cached SSR pages refresh after CMS changes.

nodes.label: CMS-Driven Static Site with Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: The site is a CMS-driven restaurant site: public pages display content from Supabase, admin pages provide CRUD for every content type (menu, hours, venue, gallery, homepage sections, signature bowls, overlay image). No hardcoded content â€” everything editable via admin.

nodes.label: Duplicate OpenTable RID Across 5 Buttons
nodes.rationale: The OpenTable widget URL with RID=325722 is copy-pasted into 5 separate booking button components (BookingCTA, HeroBookingButton, FooterBookingButton, VisitInfoBookingButton, Header). This is a consistency risk â€” changing RID requires editing 5 files.

nodes.label: Seed Data Fallback in Every API Route
nodes.rationale: Every GET route returns seed data as fallback when Supabase query fails. This mirrors the fetchers.ts pattern: try Supabase, catch â†’ return hardcoded seed. Dual-layer resilience: API routes fail to seed, fetchers also fail to seed.
nodes.norm_label: seed data fallback in every api route

nodes.label: Public Pages: Supabase or Seed Data
nodes.rationale: All public page server components call fetchers.ts functions. Each fetcher checks isSupabaseConfigured() â€” if false, returns hardcoded seed data. If true but query fails, catches error and returns seed. This means the site works without Supabase configured, showing menu/hours/venue from seed-data.ts.

nodes.label: Supabase Storage: Gallery Bucket for Image Uploads
nodes.rationale: Gallery images are uploaded to Supabase Storage 'gallery' bucket. The API generates random filenames, uploads buffers, gets public URLs, and stores metadata in gallery_images table. Delete removes both the DB record and the storage file.
nodes.norm_label: supabase storage: gallery bucket for image uploads

nodes.label: Site Settings Key-Value Store Pattern
nodes.rationale: The overlay_image_id is stored in a site_settings table as a key-value pair (key='booking_overlay_image_id'). This is a simple KV store for singleton site config â€” the only setting currently stored. Deleted when cleared.

nodes.label: Client/Server Component Boundary
nodes.rationale: Public pages are async Server Components fetching data via fetchers.ts (which uses cookies() from next/headers). Admin pages are Client Components using 'use client' with fetch() and useState/useEffect. The boundary is clean: public=SSR, admin=CSR.
